# Rule catalogue

Every rule sc4n can emit, generated from the rule registry: 206 rules, 186 of
them naming a CWE. `sc4n rules` prints the same table with the rationale for
each rule; this page exists so a reader holding a finding can look it up
without a binary, and so every rule carries a link to what to do with it.

Severity is what happens if the finding is real, confidence is how sure the
detector is; `docs/triage.md` explains how the two combine into a decision.

206 rule(s).

## The load path runs code

How to act on these: [`docs/triage.md#load-path-code`](triage.md#load-path-code).

### SC4N-JOBLIB-UNSCANNED-PAYLOAD

**joblib container is compressed with a coder sc4n cannot read** · severity `critical` · confidence `high` · class `loader` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

A file named .joblib is an xz, lzma or lz4 stream. joblib.dump pickles the object graph and joblib.load's own compressor detection reads all three, so this file is a pickle that a standard joblib.load call will decompress and deserialise — while the scanner could only report that it did not look inside. The medium SC4N-ARCHIVE-UNSUPPORTED-COMPRESSION beside it carries the algorithm and the offset; this finding states the consequence for the loader.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-JOBLIB-WRAPPER-MISMATCH

**Joblib array payload does not match the wrapper's declared shape** · severity `medium` · confidence `medium` · class `joblib` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

joblib writes an ndarray as a `NumpyArrayWrapper` (or the legacy `NDArrayWrapper`/`ZNDArrayWrapper`) pickle object followed by its payload: a one-byte padding length, that many 0xff bytes and then dtype.itemsize x count raw bytes, written into the file immediately after the wrapper and before the stream's STOP. This finding is the payload not fitting the wrapper's declared size: an inline payload that does not begin with the padding framing, or a payload a producer appended after a complete pickle whose length differs from the declared size. The gap is exactly where a second object can ride behind the array framing. Confidence is medium because joblib computes the count from the shape at load time and a wrapper the scanner cannot decode is skipped rather than guessed.

References:

- https://joblib.readthedocs.io/en/stable/persistence.html
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-LOADER-ALLOW-PICKLE

**allow_pickle=True permits object arrays to be unpickled** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `loader` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

numpy.load(..., allow_pickle=True) lets a .npy/.npz object-dtype array reach pickle.load. The array's data section is a pickle stream, so the flag re-enables the pickle RCE class on a format that is otherwise data-only.

References:

- https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.load.html


### SC4N-LOADER-JINJA-FROMSTRING

**jinja2.Environment renders a template from a string or file** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `loader` · [CWE-1336](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1336.html)

A jinja2.Environment is used with from_string/from_file in the same statement. Rendering an untrusted template with the default environment is server-side template injection; the CVE-2026-5760 SGLang RCE is this shape reached through /v1/rerank with an unsandboxed Jinja2 environment.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1336.html
- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-5760


### SC4N-LOADER-KERAS-LAMBDA

**keras.layers.Lambda constructs a layer from a Python function** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `loader` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

keras.layers.Lambda wraps a Python function (often marshalled bytecode) into a layer. A saved model containing one executes it on load, which is the Keras Lambda RCE class (VU#253266 / CVE-2024-3660).

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html
- https://kb.cert.org/vuls/id/253266


### SC4N-LOADER-KERAS-SAFE-MODE

**keras load_model is called with safe_mode=False** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `loader` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

tf.keras.models.load_model(..., safe_mode=False) disables Keras' safe-mode loading, which is the guard that refuses Lambda layers and unregistered classes. The .keras Lambda/TorchModuleWrapper rules describe what the file can then execute.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-LOADER-NO-LOCAL-ONLY

**A local model path is loaded without local_files_only** · severity `medium` · confidence `low` · class `loader` · [CWE-494](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/494.html)

An Auto* from_pretrained is given a path-shaped first argument (starting with './', '/', '~') and no local_files_only=True. If the directory is absent or incomplete the library falls back to downloading a repository of the same name, which is how a local-looking load silently becomes a remote one. Confidence is low because path-shaped strings are also used for legitimate local models.

References:

- https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main_classes/model


### SC4N-LOADER-NO-REVISION

**Model is downloaded without a pinned commit revision** · severity `medium` · confidence `medium` · class `loader` · [CWE-494](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/494.html)

from_pretrained/hf_hub_download is called with a literal model id and without a revision= argument (or with a revision that is not a 40-hex commit id). Without a pin the download follows the repository's default branch, so a later force-push changes which bytes are loaded. A call whose model argument is a variable is not reported: nothing in the source says which repository it will reach, so the finding would be about a loader function rather than about a download.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/494.html


### SC4N-LOADER-PICKLE-REMOTE

**pickle.load is called on data fetched from a network source** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `loader` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

pickle.load(s) is called on a value that came from a network or download source (urlopen, requests, socket.recv, hf_hub_download, from_pretrained). Loading a pickle from a host you did not choose is remote code execution by design.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-LOADER-TORCH-UNSAFE

**torch.load is called without weights_only=True** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `loader` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

torch.load is called with no weights_only=True (or with weights_only=False). Without the flag the loader uses the unrestricted unpickler, which executes whatever the file contains. torch 2.6 flipped the default, but a pinned older dependency, or an explicit weights_only=False, still reaches the unsafe path (CWE-502; a payload file may be a torch archive, a legacy pickle, or a 7z archive renamed .pt).

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html
- https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.load.html


### SC4N-LOADER-TRUST-REMOTE-CODE

**trust_remote_code=True enables execution of repository code** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `loader` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

trust_remote_code=True tells a Hugging Face loader to import and run Python shipped in the model repository (the auto_map path). It converts a data download into code execution and is the flag the `config.json` auto_map rule warns about from the artifact side.

References:

- https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/security


### SC4N-LOADER-YAML-UNSAFE

**yaml.load is called without a safe loader** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `loader` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

yaml.load is called with no SafeLoader/CSafeLoader (or yaml.unsafe_load is called directly). The default loader constructs arbitrary Python objects from the document, which is the PyYAML object-instantiation RCE class; yaml.safe_load is the guarded form.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-MALICE-CONSTRUCTED

**Loader runs artifact-supplied code on its own load path** · severity `critical` · confidence `high` · class `malice` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html)

The artifact's bytes are code that the loader executes while loading it, and the payload comes from the artifact itself: a pickle REDUCE hands a string to a code or process sink, a module imported through trust_remote_code calls a sink in its import-time body, or a chat template invokes a Python object that is reachable from the template context. This is the behaviour grade above the capability criticals: the same artifact's SC4N-PICKLE-GLOBAL-CRITICAL, SC4N-CONFIG-AUTO-MAP or SC4N-JINJA-PY-OBJECT finding says a sink is reachable, and this finding says which sink runs, with which payload, on the loader's own path. It does not assert intent - code that runs on load can still be benign, and the payload is quoted so a reviewer can judge it - and its absence is not a clean bill: it means the reach is structural, for example a plain attribute name on a named class, or a module that only defines classes. That third case is the capability grade and it is stated in docs/architecture.md.


### SC4N-MALICE-DEMONSTRATED

**Artifact executed on load in isolation and produced effects** · severity `critical` · confidence `high` · class `malice` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html), [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

An attestation produced by tools/sc4nconfirm recorded what happened when these exact bytes were loaded in a disposable container with no network interface and a read-only root: the process executed a program, attempted a socket connection, opened a path outside the artifact's directory, or wrote a file. The finding names the loader and the effects, and it is attributed to the artifact's SHA-256, so identical bytes scanned anywhere carry the identical verdict. sc4n never executes artifact bytes itself: this finding consumes an attestation the operator generated with a separate tool, and a scan without -attestation cannot emit it. A load that failed on an import is not a demonstration and emits nothing; the attestation records the missing module instead, so 'we could not load it' is never read as 'it did nothing'.


### SC4N-NUMPY-OBJECT-ARRAY

**Object-dtype .npy array whose data is a pickle stream** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `numpy` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

The array descriptor contains the object kind 'O', so the data section is a pickle stream rather than raw elements. Loading it requires numpy.load(..., allow_pickle=True) (the default has been False since NumPy 1.16.3), and that single flag is what turns `numpy.load` into an arbitrary-code unpickler. The data section is handed to the pickle engine, so any gadget it contains is reported under its own SC4N-PICKLE-* rule; this finding exists so the object-array detour is never invisible.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html
- https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.load.html


### SC4N-NUMPY-STRUCT

**.npy/.npz structure violates the format** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `structure` · [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html), [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

A malformed .npy header (bad magic, an unknown version, a header length past the end of the file, a dict that is not the literal {descr, fortran_order, shape} form, a negative dimension), a declared array larger than the bytes actually present, or an .npz member that cannot be read. The header is parsed with a literal reader, never eval, so a crafted header cannot execute during the scan. numpy's own loader raises on the same violations, so this is "not what the reference loader accepts" rather than an exploit.

References:

- https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.lib.format.html
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-NUMPY-TRAILING

**Bytes after the declared .npy array** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `numpy` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

The declared shape and dtype describe fewer bytes than the file contains, so there is an undeclared tail. A .npy file is exactly its header plus its array, so a tail is either an append (a polyglot or a second container) or a truncated-but-wrong rewrite. High, the same severity as every other trailing-data rule (SC4N-PICKLE-TRAILING, SC4N-SAFETENSORS-TRAILING-DATA, SC4N-XGB-UBJ-TRAILING, SC4N-GGUF-TRAILING-DATA): an undeclared tail is where a second container hides, and a memmap'd producer that leaves padding is rare enough to be worth the reader's attention.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-APPEND-TARGET

**APPEND/APPENDS targets a non-list** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

APPEND pops a value and appends it to the object beneath; the reference weights-only unpickler requires that object to be exactly a list ("Can only append to lists"). Appending into anything else either mutates an object the loader did not intend to expose or, for a class with a custom append, calls attacker-selected code. Confidence is medium because the walker cannot distinguish a list from a list subclass.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-BUILD-STATE

**BUILD applies stream-controlled state to a non-allowlisted class** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html), [CWE-915](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/915.html)

BUILD pops a state object and applies it to the value beneath it. The reference loader permits that only for torch.Tensor, torch.nn.Parameter, collections.OrderedDict and classes a user allowlisted ("Can only build Tensor, Parameter, OrderedDict or types allowlisted"). A BUILD outside that set either drives __setstate__ on an arbitrary class or, worse, sets attributes from stream data: the ShadowPickle shape is exactly `allowlisted class + payload state + BUILD`. One finding per stream reports how many distinct names are involved, with the first five listed.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/915.html
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17503


### SC4N-PICKLE-CODE-STRING

**Code-like string passed as a REDUCE argument** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

A str or bytes constant of at least 24 bytes that is passed as an argument to REDUCE, and that looks like source: `import `, `__import__`, `open(`, `os.`, `system(`, `subprocess`, `exec(`, `eval(`, `for ` with `in `, `);`. This is the rule that catches the ShadowPickle motivating stream, where the *callable is allowlisted* — `GLOBAL collections OrderedDict` plus a code string plus REDUCE plus BUILD — so nothing in a name-based policy can see it (arXiv 2607.17503). The threshold exists to keep short benign metadata strings (dtype names, sizes, small labels) out of the finding list.

References:

- https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17503
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-EXT

**Extension-registry lookup (EXT1/EXT2/EXT4)** · severity `critical` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

EXT1/EXT2/EXT4 resolve a small integer through copyreg's extension registry, which is populated by whatever the loading process imported. The opcode carries no name, so the artifact's behaviour depends on the host environment and cannot be verified statically: the same file can resolve to a benign class on one host and to a code-execution primitive on another. The weights-only unpickler does not implement these opcodes.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-GLOBAL-CRITICAL

**Pickle references a direct code-execution primitive** · severity `critical` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

The stream names a class or function that is itself a sink: the members of os/posix/nt, subprocess, pty, socket, ctypes, importlib, runpy, builtins.eval/exec/compile/__import__/open, functools.reduce, pickle.load(s), dill/cloudpickle and the rest of the table in internal/pickle/gadgets.go. `torch.load(weights_only=True)` rejects every one of these names (the allowlist is transcribed from torch/_weights_only_unpickler.py), and an unsafe `torch.load` or a bare `pickle.load` calls them. Module matching is subtree-aware, so asyncio.subprocess cannot slip past asyncio (that exact mistake was picklescan CVE-2025-10157, CVSS 8.3).

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html
- https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/v2.7.0/torch/_weights_only_unpickler.py
- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-10157


### SC4N-PICKLE-GLOBAL-HIGH

**Pickle references a reachable library gadget** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

The stream names a standard-library helper that is not a sink itself but reaches one with the right arguments: numpy.f2py.crackfortran.myeval (an eval by another name), pydoc.pipepager (a shell pipeline), logging.config._install_handlers (instantiates an arbitrary class), xmlrpc.server.resolve_dotted_attribute (resolves a dotted name and returns it), sympy.parsing.sympy_parser.eval_expr, dataclasses._create_fn (exec of generated source) and the rest of PickleCloak's published gadget set (arXiv 2508.19774, Table VI). Name-denylist scanners miss most of these. The severity is high rather than critical because the gadget needs arguments the scanner cannot always prove it has.

References:

- https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.19774
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-GLOBAL-UNKNOWN

**Pickle references a global outside the weights-only allowlist** · severity `medium` · confidence `medium` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

The stream names a class or function that is neither allowlisted by torch.load(weights_only=True) nor present in sc4n's gadget tables. Two readings are possible: an ordinary library object that the weights-only unpickler would reject (so the user must opt into the unsafe loader), or a name crafted to look ordinary. Either way the artifact cannot be loaded with weights_only=True as written. One finding per stream reports how many distinct names are involved, with the first five listed.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-INCOMPLETE

**Pickle stream could not be decoded past this offset** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `structure` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

The walker hit an opcode it could not decode — an unknown byte, a truncated or negative counted argument, or a memo reference that does not resolve — and resumed scanning byte by byte from the next position so that anything after it is still reported. This is the counter to exception-oriented programming (arXiv 2508.19774, 9 instances, 7 of them bypassing every SOTA scanner): a scanner that aborts or returns at the first error never reaches the payload, while the loader does.

References:

- https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.19774


### SC4N-PICKLE-INST

**INST constructs a class named by the stream** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

INST builds an instance of the class named in the opcode argument, calling it with the arguments on the stack. The weights-only unpickler does not implement INST at all, so a stream containing it requires the unsafe loader by construction. One finding per stream reports how many distinct names are involved, with the first five listed.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-MEMO-ALIAS

**Memo slot rebound or one name bound in several slots** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html), [CWE-694](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/694.html)

Either a memo slot is written twice, or two different slots hold the same qualified name. The reference unpickler's counterpart, torch's get_globals_in_pkl, scans a stream for names and therefore sees exactly one binding per name; a stream that binds an allowlisted name in two places, or rebinds a slot, is the ShadowPickle shape (arXiv 2607.17503) that defeats allowlist-by-name. A benign stream binds each *name* once — the class an object was built from is a different value in a different slot, and is not a second binding.

References:

- https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17503


### SC4N-PICKLE-NEWOBJ

**NEWOBJ constructs an instance of a stream-named class** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

NEWOBJ calls cls.__new__(cls, *args). The reference loader permits it only for torch.nn.Parameter and for classes in the allowlist ("Can only create new object for nn.Parameter or classes allowlisted"); anything else is a rejection, and with an attacker-chosen class in a less strict unpickler it is object construction from stream data. One finding per stream reports how many distinct names are involved, with the first five listed.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-NEWOBJ_EX

**NEWOBJ_EX constructs an instance with keyword state** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

NEWOBJ_EX is NEWOBJ with a keyword-argument state dict, which the weights-only unpickler does not implement. It is also the opcode PROTECTED_SETATTR-style payloads use, because the state dict gives the attacker control over attribute names as well as values. One finding per stream reports how many distinct names are involved, with the first five listed.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-OBJ

**OBJ constructs a class named on the stack** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

OBJ is INST with the class taken from the stack, which means the class name can be reconstructed by STACK_GLOBAL from strings. The weights-only unpickler does not implement OBJ. One finding per stream reports how many distinct names are involved, with the first five listed.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-OFFSET-ZERO

**Executable opcode at stream offset 0** · severity `critical` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

The very first byte of the stream is a GLOBAL/REDUCE-class opcode rather than the PROTO a modern pickle opens with. This is reported separately because a widely-deployed scanner bug starts its opcode scan at index 1 and therefore never sees it. The checked condition is what matters: if the first opcode introduces a global or drives a call, the payload is at offset 0 and any scanner that skips byte 0 is blind to the whole stream.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-PERSID

**Persistent id is not a ("storage", …) tuple** · severity `critical` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

PERSID/BINPERSID hand a stream-controlled id to the loader's persistent_load hook. The weights-only unpickler accepts only a tuple whose first element is "storage" (and a bare int, for old checkpoints), and its persistent_load raises unconditionally. Any other shape means the stream expects a host application to resolve an attacker-chosen identifier, which is an arbitrary-load primitive in any application that implements the hook.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-PREFIX

**Data before the pickle stream's first opcode** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

The stream does not begin with a pickle opcode: there are bytes ahead of the first PROTO/first opcode, and the payload begins after them. This is the nullifAI shape from the February 2025 Hugging Face campaign, where a broken-pickle file put its payload first and a malformed opcode after it precisely so that scanners which start at the first valid opcode see nothing. sc4n reports the leading bytes (with their entropy and any embedded native magic) and then walks the stream that follows them.

References:

- https://huggingface.co/blog/notable-models-scanned
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-REDUCE

**REDUCE calls a non-allowlisted callable** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

REDUCE pops a callable and an argument tuple and calls the callable. The reference weights-only unpickler permits this only for names in its allowlist ("Trying to call reduce for unrecognized function"), so a REDUCE over any other name is both a rejection and the point at which a pickle stream becomes a program. The per-global finding names the callable and its sink.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-REQUIRES-UNSAFE-LOADER

**Stream uses opcodes the weights-only unpickler rejects** · severity `medium` · confidence `low` · class `pickle` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

The stream contains opcodes outside the weights-only unpickler's accepted set (STACK_GLOBAL, INST, OBJ, NEWOBJ_EX, EXT1/2/4, PERSID, BINPERSID, FRAME, MEMOIZE, LONG4, BINBYTES, BINUNICODE8, BYTEARRAY8, NEXT_BUFFER, READONLY_BUFFER), so torch.load with weights_only=True cannot load it and the user must opt into the unsafe unpickler. Confidence is low and the finding says so honestly: the weights-only unpickler is protocol-2-shaped, so any protocol 4 or 5 file — including entirely benign metadata pickles written by current torch.save — trips this set. Treat it as "this artifact needs a decision", not as evidence of malice, unless another finding co-occurs.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-SAFE-GLOBALS

**Pickle requires a user allowlist entry to load weights-only** · severity `info` · confidence `medium` · class `pickle`

Every global in this stream is outside the built-in weights-only allowlist, so loading it with weights_only=True requires torch.serialization.add_safe_globals. That is a deliberate act by the user, and the names involved appear in the SC4N-PICKLE-GLOBAL-UNKNOWN summary; this finding exists so that a reader can see the artifact's loading requirement as a single fact rather than reconstructing it from the per-global findings. The ID is historical and reads like a clearance; it is not one — the Title is the statement.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-SEGMENT

**Concatenated pickle segments** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

STOP is not end-of-file: the bytes after it start another complete pickle, so the file holds several segments (joblib, legacy torch checkpoints and stacked-pickle files all do this legitimately). sc4n walks and reports every segment. The finding is informational on its own; read the segments' own findings, because a payload in the second segment is exactly how a scanner that reads one pickle per file misses it.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-SETITEM-TARGET

**SETITEM/SETITEMS targets a non-dict** · severity `critical` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-787](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/787.html), [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

SETITEM and SETITEMS assign into the object beneath them. The reference weights-only unpickler performs `self.stack[-1][k] = v` without checking the target's type, which is the heap-corruption class CVE-2026-24747 / GHSA-63cw-57p8-fm3p fixed in torch 2.10.0 by adding the check. A stream whose SETITEM target is not a dict therefore corrupts memory on a 2.7-era loader and is rejected by a fixed one.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/787.html
- https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/security/advisories/GHSA-63cw-57p8-fm3p


### SC4N-PICKLE-STACK

**Operand stack exceeded MaxStackDepth** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `limits` · [CWE-674](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/674.html)

The stream pushes more values than the stack budget allows, so the walk stopped at the cap and the remainder was not analysed. A real torch state_dict builds a stack a few hundred entries deep; a stream that exceeds a million is either an accident or an attempt to exhaust the scanner before it reaches the payload.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/674.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-STRUCT

**Pickle stream violates the opcode grammar** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `structure` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html), [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)

An unknown opcode, an argument that a declared protocol cannot carry, a truncated or negative counted length, a missing STOP, a memo or stack reference that does not resolve, or a non-UTF-8 payload inside a unicode opcode. The extra field names the specific violation. Structurally invalid pickles are the IDS-evasion family of arXiv 2508.15987 (PickleBall): the stream is still executed by the loader while a scanner that stops at the first error sees nothing beyond it, which is why sc4n reports the violation and keeps walking.

References:

- https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.15987
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-PICKLE-TRAILING

**Data after the pickle stream's STOP** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `pickle` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

Bytes follow a complete pickle and do not themselves start a pickle. The reference unpickler stops at the first STOP, so nothing legitimate is there, while any reader that loops over load() — joblib, a legacy torch archive, a hand-rolled loader — executes what follows. This is the other half of the nullifAI broken-pickle shape and the mechanism behind scanner-bypassing stacked-pickle files.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-TORCH-7Z

**7z archive disguised as a PyTorch checkpoint** · severity `critical` · confidence `high` · class `torch` · [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html)

The artifact's name says it is a torch checkpoint (.pt/.pth/.ckpt/.ptl/.pt2) but its bytes begin with the 7z signature 37 7A BC AF 27 1C. This is the February 2025 Hugging Face campaign: a patched loader still deserialised the payload while every extension-driven scanner saw "not a zip". sc4n cannot decode 7z (no stdlib decoder) and says so with SC4N-ARCHIVE-UNSUPPORTED-COMPRESSION; the pickle inside is NOT scanned.

References:

- https://huggingface.co/blog/notable-models-scanned
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html


### SC4N-TORCH-LEGACY

**PyTorch legacy binary checkpoint recognised** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `torch` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

The artifact is a legacy PyTorch checkpoint (written by _legacy_save, i.e. _use_new_zipfile_serialization=False or any pre-1.6 torch): a pickled MAGIC_NUMBER, then PROTOCOL_VERSION, sys_info, the object pickle and the storage_keys pickle, followed by raw storage bytes. Each leading pickle is walked individually with the storage tail treated as storage, so a child-checkpoint's appended storage is not misreported as an attack suffix.

References:

- https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/serialization.html


### SC4N-TORCH-LEGACY-TAR

**PyTorch legacy tar checkpoint recognised** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `torch` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

The artifact is a legacy tar checkpoint with the members storages, tensors and pickle. The pickle member is the object graph and is handed to the pickle engine; storages and tensors begin with metadata pickles and then carry raw storage bytes, which are treated as storage.

References:

- https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.19774


### SC4N-TORCH-PREFIXED-ARCHIVE

**PyTorch archive has bytes before the zip local header** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `torch` · [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html)

The artifact is a valid zip whose first byte is not PK\x03\x04: arbitrary bytes precede the first local file header. Python's _is_zipfile only checks the current offset, but the C++ PyTorchStreamReader initialises miniz over the whole byte range and derives the archive prefix from the first record, so the loader still deserialises the payload while an offset-sensitive scanner reports "not a zip". sc4n unwraps it and scans every member.

References:

- https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/serialization.html


### SC4N-TORCH-PT2

**PyTorch .pt2 export archive recognised** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `torch` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

The artifact is a .pt2 export archive (zip with archive_format + models/<m>.json + data/weights + data/sample_inputs). data/sample_inputs/*.pt are genuine torch.save pickles and data/constants/custom_obj_* are TorchBind objects, so both reach the pickle engine; any *.wrapper.so member is native code and is reported by the archive layer as SC4N-ARCHIVE-NATIVE-MEMBER.

References:

- https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/export.html


### SC4N-TORCH-SCRIPT

**TorchScript archive recognised** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `torch` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

The artifact is a TorchScript archive: a zip carrying data.pkl plus constants.pkl and/or code/**/*.py. The code/*.py members are valid Python stored as *data* and are attacker-controlled, so they are handed to the Python analyser; data.pkl, constants.pkl and *.debug_pkl are handed to the pickle engine.

References:

- https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/jit.html


### SC4N-TORCH-STRUCT

**Torch checkpoint structure is malformed** · severity `medium` · confidence `medium` · class `torch` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

A torch container's structure does not match its declared shape: the legacy magic or protocol-version pickle is missing, a leading pickle did not reach a STOP, or a section of the file could not be carved as a pickle. A loader that tolerates the same malformation may still execute the payload, so this is a finding rather than a reason to skip the file.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-TORCH-ZIP

**PyTorch new-format archive (zip) recognised** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `torch` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

The artifact is a PyTorch new-format checkpoint: an uncompressed zip whose first local file header is PK\x03\x04 and whose members are data.pkl, byteorder and data/<n> storages. data.pkl is a Python pickle and is analysed by the pickle engine; the rule exists so a reader can see which torch shape was recognised rather than inferring it from the absence of findings.

References:

- https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/serialization.html

## Code the repository ships

How to act on these: [`docs/triage.md#shipped-code`](triage.md#shipped-code).

### SC4N-ADAPTER-EXTERNAL-BASE

**PEFT adapter resolves its base model to another repository** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `adapter` · [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html)

A PEFT `adapter_config.json` sets `base_model_name_or_path` to a value that does not resolve to a directory in the scanned tree — a Hub repository id or a URL. Loading the adapter therefore downloads and loads a *second* artifact whose contents are not in this scan, so an adapter that looks benign can pull in a base model the user never reviewed. High because the indirection is the point: the scan's verdict is incomplete without the referenced repository, and the name is the only thing sc4n can check.

References:

- https://huggingface.co/docs/peft/main/en/package_reference/config
- https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/security


### SC4N-CODE-AGENT-CODE-EXEC

**Agent is constructed with a code executor** · severity `medium` · confidence `medium` · class `code` · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

The source builds an agent (Agent, LlmAgent, AgentTool) whose tools include a code executor (BuiltInCodeExecutor, code_executor=/CodeExecutor) and that also exposes an MCP session, a retrieval corpus or HTTP requests. Together they describe an agent that can be driven to execute code and to reach the network, so the artifact's behaviour depends on inputs it fetches at run time rather than on the code in the file.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html


### SC4N-CODE-COMPILE-EXEC

**compile() is called with an exec mode** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `code` · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

compile(source, filename, mode) is called with mode 'exec' (or a mode string containing it), which compiles a whole module body rather than a single expression. It is the explicit form of the exec() pattern and is rare in ordinary model-loading code.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html


### SC4N-CODE-ENCODED-PAYLOAD

**A long encoded literal is decoded in the same statement** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `code` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

A base64- or hex-shaped literal of at least 32 characters appears in a statement that also calls a decoder (base64.b64decode, codecs.decode, bytes.fromhex, binascii.*, zlib). The pairing is the standard second-stage shape: the literal alone is opaque data and the decoder alone is ordinary library use.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1336.html


### SC4N-CODE-NOTEBOOK-MAGIC

**Notebook cell uses an IPython magic or shell escape** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `code` · [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

A code cell runs an IPython magic or a shell escape: `!cmd`, `%%bash`, `%%sh`, `%%javascript`, `%%html`, `%%writefile`, `%run` or `%system`. These are executed by the notebook kernel (the `!`/`%%bash` forms through a shell), so they are not visible to a Python lexer's ordinary rules and a notebook that looks like harmless Python can still spawn a process when opened and run. The finding reports the line in the .ipynb file, not in the cell.

References:

- https://ipython.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactive/magics.html


### SC4N-CODE-OBFUSCATION

**Code is assembled from obfuscated string or character fragments** · severity `medium` · confidence `medium` · class `code` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

The statement builds a string from obfuscated pieces: a chain of chr() calls, a "".join([...]) of many literals, a long run of \x escapes, a long bytes([...]) literal, or an f-string with nested replacement fields. Each is a way to keep a command out of the readable text a reviewer greps for; the finding names which construct was seen.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1336.html


### SC4N-CODE-REDUCE-BUILDER

**Python source builds a pickle payload with __reduce__** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `code` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

A class in this file defines __reduce__ or __reduce_ex__ returning a callable that executes code (eval, exec, os.system, subprocess.*, __import__, marshal.loads, pickle.loads, ctypes.*) together with a serialiser dump (pickle/dill/cloudpickle/joblib dump, torch.save). The pair is what a pickle payload generator looks like: the class is inert until something unpickles the file it was dumped into, so the generator is the human-readable half of the attack.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html


### SC4N-CODE-REMOTE-TOOL-LOADER

**Python source loads and runs code from a Hub repository** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `code` · [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

transformers.load_tool('org/repo') resolves a Space or repository from the Hub and imports its Python module into the current process, so the repository's code runs with the caller's privileges. A model card cannot make that code inspectable: the trust decision is delegated to whoever controls the named repository, at whatever revision it currently has.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html


### SC4N-CODE-REVERSE-SHELL

**Python source contains a reverse-shell shape** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `code` · [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html), [CWE-306](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/306.html)

One artifact contains a socket constructor, a connect call, a receive call and a command sink (subprocess.*, os.system, os.popen). Each of those alone is ordinary; together they describe a connection that receives commands and runs them, which is the interactive access payload a model file or a training script carries. The markers are matched over the whole artifact, because a generator that embeds the payload in a string literal carries the same signal as one that runs it.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/306.html

shutil.rmtree/os.remove/os.unlink/os.rmdir/os.rename/shutil.move is called with a path derived from an external source, so the caller controls which file is removed or moved.

### SC4N-CODE-TAINT-DESERIALIZE

**Data from an untrusted source is deserialised** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `code` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

A value derived from an external source is passed to pickle.load(s), dill/cloudpickle, marshal.loads, torch.load, or yaml.load/unsafe_load. Deserialising attacker-influenced bytes is the pickle RCE class (CWE-502); the loader-safety family flags the same calls when they are missing their guard.

### SC4N-CODE-TAINT-DYNAMIC

**Attribute name is resolved from an untrusted source** · severity `high` · confidence `low` · class `code` · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

getattr/setattr/delattr is called with a name derived from an external source, which lets the caller select which attribute (or method) is reached. Confidence is low because the same pattern is common in legitimate plugin code; read the source value before acting on it.

### SC4N-CODE-TAINT-EXEC

**Data from an untrusted source reaches a code-execution sink** · severity `critical` · confidence `medium` · class `code` · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

A value derived from an external source (input, argv, environment, a file or socket read, a decoded blob, a downloaded model) is passed to exec/eval/compile/__import__, importlib.import_module, runpy, a ctypes native-library load, or an interactive interpreter. The taint is statement-level and intra-function: sc4n does not model containers, aliases or closure capture, so a finding is an upper bound on risk and a clean result is not a proof.

**A file is written to a path derived from an untrusted source** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `code` · [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html), [CWE-73](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/73.html)

open() is called in a writing mode ('w'/'a'/'x') with a path derived from an external source, so the caller controls where bytes land (path traversal / arbitrary write). The mode is read from the second positional argument or the mode= keyword.

A value derived from an external source is sent through requests/httpx/urllib, webbrowser.open, or a socket connect. Inside a model script this is the exfiltration half of the credential-shaped rules: the value is usually a token read from the environment or the Hugging Face cache.
