### SC4N-SAFETENSORS-STRUCT

**safetensors header violates a structural invariant** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `format` · [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)

The header does not satisfy one of the invariants the reference safetensors loader enforces before returning any tensor: the declared header length is within the 100 MB cap, the file is at least 8+header bytes long, the header is valid UTF-8 JSON beginning with '{', '__metadata__' maps strings to strings, every other top-level key is a tensor entry of {dtype, shape, data_offsets} with no duplicate keys, shapes are integers, END >= BEGIN, offsets tile the byte buffer with no overlap and no hole, and product(shape)*bitsize/8 equals the declared span and is byte-aligned. The reference sorts the tensor list by data_offsets before checking contiguity, so document order is not itself an invariant: a header that lists a later tensor first is accepted. A negative data_offsets element is rejected because the reference types the pair as (usize, usize). safetensors has no published advisories and the reference loader fails closed on every one of these, so the finding means the file is malformed for the reference loader -- the shape that matters when something other than the reference loader reads it.

References:

- https://github.com/huggingface/safetensors
- https://github.com/huggingface/safetensors/blob/main/safetensors/src/tensor.rs


### SC4N-SAFETENSORS-TRAILING-DATA

**Bytes follow the last declared tensor** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `format` · [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)

The last tensor's data_offsets end before the end of the byte buffer, so the file carries bytes the safetensors format has no field for. The reference loader computes coverage and rejects such a file, so this is not a loader-reachable payload in the reference implementation -- it is the polyglot/steganography shape: an appended native executable, a second serialisation or an obfuscated blob that a looser reader, a hex editor or a smuggled re-write would expose. Severity is high rather than critical precisely because the reference loader fails closed.

References:

- https://github.com/huggingface/safetensors/blob/main/safetensors/src/tensor.rs


### SC4N-SAFETENSORS-TRUNCATED

**Declared header or tensor extent runs past the end of the file** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `format` · [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)

The file is shorter than its 8-byte header length declares, or a tensor's data_offsets reach past the end of the byte buffer. The reference loader fails closed on both. The finding is recorded rather than treated as an unreadable file because a truncated model is the shape a partially downloaded or deliberately clipped artifact takes, and a scanner that reports nothing for it is indistinguishable from one that found nothing.

References:

- https://github.com/huggingface/safetensors/blob/main/safetensors/src/tensor.rs


### SC4N-TF-ASSET-EXECUTABLE

**SavedModel assets directory holds an executable or script** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `code` · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

A file under a SavedModel's assets/ or assets.extra/ directory is a native executable (validated ELF/PE/Mach-O header) or carries a shell shebang. assets/ exists to carry files the graph names at run time, and TF's own asset ops (ReadFile, MatchingFiles) reach it, so an executable parked there is either a loader path the model names or a stub the surrounding deployment runs.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-TF-CHECKPOINT-NO-CODE

**TensorFlow checkpoint carries no inline code** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `content`

The artifact is a bare TensorFlow checkpoint (.index / .data shards), which stores tensor variables and no graph and no inline code, so there is nothing here for sc4n to execute and no code to find. This note exists so a clean verdict is not misread as "safe to load blindly": a checkpoint is only as trustworthy as the code that names its variables and runs it.

References:

- https://www.tensorflow.org/guide/checkpoint


### SC4N-TF-CHECKPOINT-STRUCT

**TensorFlow checkpoint index is malformed** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `structure` · [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)

A .index file does not begin with a plausible BundleHeaderProto: its first field is not a varint shard count, or a later field runs past the end of the file. The structure is only outlined (v1 does not rebuild the object graph), so the note is about what was and was not checked.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html


### SC4N-TF-FILE-IO

**TensorFlow op reads or writes an out-of-tree path** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `path` · [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html), [CWE-73](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/73.html)

A SavedModel/GraphDef contains a file-IO op (ReadFile/WriteFile/SaveV2/RestoreV2/ReaderRead*/MatchingFiles/FileName) whose path constant is absolute, contains a '..' segment, uses a drive letter or UNC prefix, is a URL or starts with '~'. The loader reads or writes that path when the graph runs, so the artifact is a file-access primitive rather than a model.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html


### SC4N-TF-PYFUNC

**TensorFlow graph calls an arbitrary Python function** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `code` · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

A SavedModel/GraphDef contains a PyFunc or EagerPyFunc op. Executing the graph calls the registered Python function that the op names, on data the graph controls, so the model is not a pure data-flow artifact: a native op that performs file or network IO can be reached from a model file. Confirm the named token is one the deployment registered deliberately.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html


### SC4N-TF-STRUCT

**TensorFlow protobuf is truncated or malformed** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `structure` · [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)

A SavedModel/GraphDef protobuf has a field whose declared length runs past the end of the message, or a wire type its declaration cannot carry. The walk stopped at that point and reports how far it got, rather than treating a parse failure as an absence of findings.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html


### SC4N-TFJS-FLEX-OP

**TensorFlow-JS graph uses a Flex op** · severity `medium` · confidence `medium` · class `code` · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

A TF-JS model.json graph (or a TF GraphDef carried as JSON) names a Flex-prefixed op. Flex ops delegate to TensorFlow's C++ kernels rather than the portable JS kernel set, so executing the graph requires a runtime that links the full TF native library, which is a much larger attack surface than the model's own op set implies.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html


### SC4N-TFLITE-CUSTOM-OP

**TFLite model declares a custom operator** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `code` · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

A TFLite model names a custom operator (a non-empty custom_code, builtin_code CUSTOM, or a custom_options blob). A custom op has no implementation in the model: the runtime resolves the name to a device plugin it has already loaded, so the model's behaviour is decided by native code outside the artifact. A model that requires one is not portable data.

References:

- https://www.tensorflow.org/lite/guide/ops_custom


### SC4N-TFLITE-ENTROPY

**TFLite buffer has compressed or encrypted entropy** · severity `info` · confidence `low` · class `content`

A TFLite buffer's byte entropy is at or above 7.9 bits/byte, which says the region looks compressed, encrypted or randomly padded rather than like quantised weights. This is informational only: quantised weights can legitimately look random, so it is a pointer for a reviewer, not a finding that changes the verdict.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-TFLITE-NATIVE-MAGIC

**TFLite model embeds a native executable in a buffer** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `code` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

A TFLite buffer holds a validated native executable (ELF/PE/Mach-O header) rather than tensor data. TFLite buffers are model weights; an executable among them is a payload the format has no reason to carry, and the shape used to smuggle native code past a data-only scanner.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-TFLITE-STRUCT

**TFLite flatbuffer header or table is malformed** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `structure` · [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)

A .tflite file's root table offset or a vtable/vector/string reference points outside the file, or the identifier is not 'TFL3' at offset 4. The walk reports the broken reference — once per file, so a malformed file cannot spend the whole finding budget on its own damage — and continues wherever the remaining structure is resolvable, so the parts that are readable are still walked.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html


### SC4N-TRT-UNVERIFIED

**TensorRT engine is recognised but not deep-parsed** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `format`

The file starts with the `ftrt` magic of a TensorRT serialized engine. sc4n does not interpret the section table (the format is versioned and NVIDIA does not publish a stable specification), so the finding states the depth instead of implying the file is clean: the indicator engine covered the first 4 MiB and the last 1 MiB only, and the serialized weights between those windows were not scanned. A payload hidden in the weight region is out of scope.


### SC4N-XGB-UBJ-STRUCT

**UBJSON stream is structurally invalid or exceeds the walk budget** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `format` · [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)

The XGBoost UBJSON value stream could not be walked: an unknown marker, a length or count that is negative or exceeds the bytes actually remaining, a typed container without the mandatory count, or an unsupported typed element. A container over the element budget is reported separately, as SC4N-LIMIT-ENTRIES naming MaxArrayElements. The parse stops at the first unrecoverable point and the walk is bounded throughout, so an attacker-controlled length is never allocated. A malformed model means an XGBoost reader and sc4n disagree about where the document ends, which is how appended data hides.

References:

- https://ubjson.org/type-reference/
- https://github.com/dmlc/xgboost/blob/master/src/common/json.cc


### SC4N-XGB-UBJ-TRAILING

**Bytes follow the root UBJSON value** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `polyglot` · [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)

The UBJSON parse completed a root value and then found more bytes. XGBoost's reader decodes exactly one root value and ignores whatever follows, so the trailing region is invisible to the legitimate loader while remaining visible to any other reader that is handed the file. That is the polyglot/smuggling shape: an appended executable, a second container, or a serialised object. The XGBoost documentation itself states the in-memory snapshot is not secure, so do not assume the trailing bytes are benign just because the model part parsed.

References:

- https://ubjson.org/type-reference/
- https://github.com/dmlc/xgboost/blob/master/doc/tutorials/saving_model.rst

## Content, text and persuasion

How to act on these: [`docs/triage.md#content-persuasion`](triage.md#content-persuasion).

### SC4N-CARD-COMMENT

**Card carries an HTML comment with no instruction in it** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `card` · [CWE-1007](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1007.html)

A model card, dataset card or metadata value contains an HTML comment whose body carries no instruction-shaped text. A Markdown renderer drops the comment, so the reader never sees it, which is why it is reported at all; it is informational because a commented-out heading, a `<!-- markdownlint-disable -->` directive and an uploader's `<!-- RVN_FILE_SELECTION_GUIDE_START -->` markers are ordinary editorial practice — 419 of the 450 comments in the 273-model HF campaign. A comment that does carry instruction-shaped text is SC4N-CARD-HIDDEN (high).

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1007.html
- https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/model-cards


### SC4N-CARD-HIDDEN

**Card hides instruction text in an HTML comment or reorders text with control characters** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `card` · [CWE-1007](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1007.html), [CWE-1426](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1426.html)

A model card, dataset card or metadata value carries instruction-shaped text inside an HTML comment, or a run of order-affecting control characters (the bidirectional overrides and directional marks — Trojan Source). Every Markdown renderer drops HTML comments, so an instruction in one is present for the model and absent for the person reviewing the card, and a bidirectional override reorders what that person reads. High because text shaped like an instruction, or a character that rewrites the reading order, has no editorial purpose in a card. A comment *without* instruction-shaped text is SC4N-CARD-COMMENT (info) and a zero-width run that reorders nothing is SC4N-CARD-INVISIBLE (medium): the split is what keeps this rule's severity meaningful on the 450 comments and invisible runs of the 273-model HF campaign, every one of which carried no instruction at all.

References:

- https://trojansource.codes/
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1007.html
- https://owasp.org/www-project-top-10-for-large-language-model-applications/


### SC4N-CARD-INJECTION

**Card or metadata carries an instruction aimed at a model** · severity `medium` · confidence `medium` · class `card` · [CWE-1426](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1426.html)

A model card, dataset card or metadata value contains a directive aimed at a model rather than at a reader: an imperative ("you must", "always respond", "never reveal"), a tool/function-call JSON directive ("tool_calls", "function_call", "recipient_name", <tool_call>), or instruction-like text hidden inside an HTML comment. Cards and metadata are pasted into prompts by agents and by RAG pipelines, so text in them is an input channel with no executable artifact required (OWASP LLM01). Medium because a document that discusses prompt injection, and a legitimate README that says "you must install the dependencies", contain similar words; read the evidence. This rule is medium where SC4N-TEMPLATE-INJECTION is high for the same phrasing: a card is read once, by whoever opens it, while a chat template is rendered around every conversation the model serves.

References:

- https://owasp.org/www-project-top-10-for-large-language-model-applications/
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1426.html


### SC4N-CARD-INVISIBLE

**Card carries an invisible character that reorders nothing** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `card` · [CWE-1007](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1007.html)

A model card, dataset card or metadata value contains a run of zero-width or soft-hyphen characters: characters a reader does not see, but that do not reorder the text either. Medium because copy-paste from a rendered page carries them by accident — they are also legitimate data in a tokenizer vocabulary — where an order-affecting control character is never accidental and is reported as SC4N-CARD-HIDDEN (high).

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1007.html


### SC4N-CARD-PARSE

**Card frontmatter could not be parsed and was scanned as raw text** · severity `low` · confidence `high` · class `card` · [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)

A card's YAML frontmatter block is malformed — an unclosed block, a top-level line with no key, or a list item with no enclosing key — so its fields could not be resolved by name. sc4n does not link a YAML library and does not need one to scan text, so the document is still scanned in full as raw text; this finding records that the structured view is missing, which matters when a reviewer is comparing the frontmatter fields against what the scanner saw. A nested mapping is *not* reported: it is valid YAML this subset does not model, and the standard model-index block of an evaluated card is exactly that shape.

References:

- https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/model-cards


### SC4N-CONTENT-EICAR

**Antivirus test file (EICAR) is present** · severity `low` · confidence `high` · class `content`

The artifact contains the 68-byte EICAR antivirus test string. It is not malware: it is the industry's scanner self-test, and its presence means the file is a deliberate AV test sample (or a container that embeds one), which every antivirus product quarantines. Reported so a corpus is not read as clean when it ships a scanner test artifact.

References:

- https://www.eicar.org/download-anti-malware-testfile/


### SC4N-CONTENT-NOT-UTF8

**Text artifact is not valid UTF-8** · severity `low` · confidence `high` · class `content` · [CWE-838](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/838.html)

The artifact was classified as text (its first kilobyte holds no NUL byte) but its bytes are not valid UTF-8, so the text-only layers did not run: the model-card injection detector, the tokenizer analyser, the Jinja2 analyser and the Unicode-anomaly pass all require a valid UTF-8 document. The byte-level indicators (the literal table, the raw-IP URL hunt and the obfuscation pass) did run over the whole buffer and are reported alongside this finding. The offset of the first invalid byte is in the finding's extra data. Re-encode the file as UTF-8 to have the remaining layers applied.


### SC4N-CONTENT-UTF16

**Text artifact was UTF-16 and was decoded before scanning** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `format`

The artifact's bytes are UTF-16 text (a byte-order mark, or ASCII interleaved with NUL bytes). Every content heuristic in sc4n is byte-oriented, so the undecoded file looks binary: the text sniffer does not see prose, the model-card analyser never runs and the indicator engine reads the interleaving as data. sc4n decoded the whole file to UTF-8 and re-dispatched it, so format sniffing, the card analyser and the indicator engine all read the text. Offsets in findings on the decoded text are offsets into the decoded bytes. This finding is informational and exists so that a clean report is read as "decoded and scanned".

References:

- https://www.unicode.org/faq/utf_bom.html


### SC4N-IMG-METADATA

**Image metadata was read and scanned** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `format`

The artifact is a PNG or JPEG image and sc4n read its text metadata (PNG tEXt, zTXt, iTXt and eXIf chunks; JPEG APP1 Exif, APP1 XMP and COM segments) and ran every string through the shared indicator engine and the invisible-character pass. The pixels and any entropy-coded data are not decoded, so a payload hidden in pixel data (steganography) is not covered. This finding is informational and exists so that a clean image report is read as "metadata read, nothing in it" rather than "not recognised".

References:

- https://www.w3.org/TR/png-3/
- https://www.cipa.jp/std/documents/e/DC-008-Translation-2019-E.pdf


### SC4N-IMG-STRUCT

**Image metadata framing is invalid** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `format` · [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)

A PNG chunk or JPEG segment carrying metadata does not satisfy its own framing: a declared length runs past the end of the file, the chunk list ends without an IEND, a JPEG marker stream loses its alignment before SOS, an iTXt/zTXt compression method is not the defined deflate, or a zlib stream does not inflate. A reader that trusts the declared length reads a different byte range than sc4n inspected, so the mismatch is reported rather than treated as a parse detail; the metadata that could be read before the break is still scanned.

References:

- https://www.w3.org/TR/png-3/
- https://www.cipa.jp/std/documents/e/DC-008-Translation-2019-E.pdf


### SC4N-METADATA-CODE

**Metadata value contains code-execution keywords** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `metadata` · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

A metadata value — a tensor name, a __metadata__ entry, a GGUF key, an ONNX doc_string or a config field — contains code-execution keywords: os.system, subprocess, __import__, exec, eval, pickle.load, marshal.loads, socket.socket, urllib.request, requests.post or a base64 decode. Metadata is read (and sometimes printed, templated or executed) by tooling, so a value that is source code is a different kind of object than the field it occupies claims to be.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html


### SC4N-METADATA-INJECTION

**Data string contains prompt-injection phrasing** · severity `medium` · confidence `medium` · class `metadata` · [CWE-1426](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1426.html)

A string in the artifact contains instruction-like text aimed at a model rather than at a reader: "ignore previous instructions", "ignore the above", "do not tell the user", "override your instructions", an exfiltration instruction. Model cards, dataset cards and metadata are read by agents and are pasted into prompts, so text in them is an input channel into whatever consumes the artifact (OWASP LLM01). The chat-format delimiters themselves ([INST], <|im_start|>, <system>, ### Instruction:) are not indicators: a card that documents a chat template, a tokenizer that declares its own control token and a template file that prints them all contain those bytes without asking a model to do anything, and they were 157 of the 172 findings on the 273-model campaign. The above-anaphora family ("ignore the above instructions", "disregard the above", "forget the above") is what an instruction that overrides the text before it looks like when it is prepended to a prompt. The rule is medium because a document that quotes an injection, or a legitimate chat template, contains the same literals.

References:

- https://owasp.org/www-project-top-10-for-large-language-model-applications/
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1426.html


### SC4N-STRING-C2

**Data string names a command-and-control or exfiltration endpoint** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `content` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

A string in the artifact contains a webhook, paste, tunnel or overlay endpoint: discord.com/api/webhooks, api.telegram.org, hooks.slack.com, webhook.site, requestbin, pipedream, canarytokens, interact.sh and the other oast domains, transfer.sh, ngrok, trycloudflare, serveo, or a .onion address. These are how a payload that runs inside a loader gets its instructions or sends what it found out. The indicator is a literal match, so a document that *discusses* webhook abuse trips it too; read the offset before concluding.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html
- https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/


### SC4N-STRING-CREDENTIAL

**Data string names credential material or a credential path** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `content` · [CWE-522](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/522.html), [CWE-200](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html)

A string in the artifact references a credential store or *reads* a credential from the environment: ~/.ssh and the files under it, ~/.aws/credentials, the Hugging Face token cache, /etc/shadow, /proc/self/environ, .netrc, .git-credentials, .docker/config.json, .kube/config, or a shell/batch expansion or environment lookup of AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, HF_TOKEN and their relatives. A model artifact has no functional reason to reach for any of these. The rule distinguishes a *use* from a mention: the bare name of a credential environment variable is not an indicator (a tool schema or a deployment note naming GITHUB_TOKEN is describing which variables exist, not reading one), and a bare credential file name (id_rsa, known_hosts, credentials.json) is reported only beside a decoder or second-stage callable — a GCP guide that names credentials.json, or an SSH guide that names known_hosts, is not reaching for it.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/522.html


### SC4N-STRING-DECODER

**Data string names a decoder or a second-stage loader** · severity `medium` · confidence `medium` · class `content` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

A string in the artifact names a decoding or second-stage-loading call: base64 and hex decoders, the compression decompressors, marshal.loads, compile/exec/eval, __import__, os.system, subprocess.Popen, or a second pickle/dill/cloudpickle load. Any one of these in a metadata value is an obfuscation or second-stage indicator; the combination of a long opaque literal and a decoder in the same string is what SC4N-STRING-OBFUSCATION reports.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-STRING-LOADER-FLAG

**Data string sets a flag that turns off a loader's safety** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `content` · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

A data string sets trust_remote_code=true, allow_pickle=True, weights_only=False, safe_mode=False, yaml.unsafe_load or load_in_8bit, or calls yaml.load. Each of these is a documented way to make a loader execute code that the artifact supplies, and a config that carries one is telling the loader to disable the check that would have stopped it. The bare name of a flag is not reported: `auto_map` as a key and `trust_remote_code` as a key are the field names of ordinary configuration, and the document-level decision they encode belongs to SC4N-CONFIG-AUTO-MAP and SC4N-CONFIG-TRUST-REMOTE-CODE, which can state whether the referenced module is present.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html
- https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/security


### SC4N-STRING-OBFUSCATION

**Data string hides a long opaque literal beside a decoder** · severity `medium` · confidence `medium` · class `content` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

A string in the artifact contains a long base64 or hexadecimal literal (at least 48 characters) and, in the same string or an adjacent one, a decoder call. The combination is the standard way to carry a second-stage payload past a scanner that looks for readable commands: the literal alone is ordinary data, and the decoder alone is ordinary library usage. The rule reports the literal's length and offset, not its contents.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-STRING-RAW-IP-URL

**Data string contains a URL with a raw IP address** · severity `medium` · confidence `medium` · class `content` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

A string in the artifact contains an http/https URL whose host is a literal IP address rather than a name (http://192.0.2.10:8080/payload). Legitimate model metadata points at named hosts: a raw IP in a data file means either an ad-hoc server or an attempt to bypass name-based blocking, and it is one of the few endpoint shapes a domain denylist cannot cover. Every notation a client resolves counts, not only the dotted decimal one: hex octets (http://0x7f.0.0.1/), octal octets (http://0177.0.0.1/) and a single 32-bit number in decimal, octal or hex (http://2130706433/, http://017700000001/, http://0x7f000001/) all reach a host, and the finding's form names the notation it saw.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-STRING-SECRET-VALUE

**Data string contains what looks like a hard-coded secret** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `content` · [CWE-798](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html), [CWE-540](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/540.html)

A string in the artifact assigns a value to a credential variable (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=, GITHUB_TOKEN=, OPENAI_API_KEY=, HF_TOKEN=, password=, api_key=, …), contains a PEM private-key header, or carries a credential that announces its own vendor: a GitHub token (ghp_, github_pat_), a Hugging Face token (hf_), an OpenAI key (sk-), an AWS access key id (AKIA, ASIA), a Google API key (AIza), a Slack token (xoxb-) or a JSON Web Token (eyJ… with three dot-separated segments). The matched value is masked: the finding records that a secret-shaped string is present and where, without reproducing it into a log, a SARIF upload or a baseline file. Note the direction of the risk this does not cover: a secret committed by an honest author is a leak, while a secret read by a malicious one is exfiltration, and this rule cannot tell them apart.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html


### SC4N-STRING-SHELL

**Data string contains a shell or process payload** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `content` · [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html)

A string in the artifact contains a shell payload fragment: an interactive shell (bash -i, /bin/sh -c), a pipe into an interpreter (curl | sh, wget -qO-), a reverse shell (nc -e, /dev/tcp/, socat exec:), a PowerShell or cmd encoder invocation, or a download-and-run chain. These carry their own context and are reported wherever they appear. The interpreter-invocation fragments that are also ordinary install-document words (chmod +x, python -c, perl -e, base64 -d, whoami, mkfifo) are reported only when the same string also names a decoder or second-stage callable, which is the decoder-chain shape; naming one in a README is not a finding.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html


### SC4N-TOKENIZER-REDOS

**Tokenizer regex is not expressible in RE2 and can backtrack catastrophically** · severity `medium` · confidence `medium` · class `tokenizer` · [CWE-1333](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1333.html)

A regular expression inside tokenizer.json uses a construct that RE2 does not support and that a backtracking engine can make super-linear: a backreference (\1, \k<>, (?P=name)), a lookaround ((?=), (?!), (?<=), (?<!)), an atomic group ((?>)), a recursion or subroutine call ((?R), (?0), (?&name), (?P>name)), a conditional group ((?(...))), a possessive quantifier (*+, ++, ?+), or a quantified group that already contains a quantifier ((\w+)+, (a*)*). The Rust `tokenizers` crate runs these through an RE2-family engine where the pattern is simply an error, but the Python implementations hand the same pattern to `re`/`regex`, where it is a denial-of-service hazard on attacker-influenced input (the CVE-2024-12720 / CVE-2025-2099 / CVE-2025-3263 / CVE-2025-5197 family). Severity is medium and the construct is named: the pattern is legitimate in some distributions, and the finding assumes Python-regex semantics.

References:

- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-12720
- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-2099
- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-3263
- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-5197
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1333.html


### SC4N-TOKENIZER-UNKNOWN-CLASS

**tokenizer_class is outside the known Transformers tokenizer set** · severity `info` · confidence `low` · class `tokenizer` · [CWE-1357](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1357.html)

A tokenizer_class is not one of the classes Transformers ships. That is often an entirely ordinary custom tokenizer, but a class name the local library does not know is also how a repository routes loading through code the user did not intend to run (the same shape as an auto_map entry). Informational: the name is recorded so a reviewer can check whether the named class resolves to a library the user already has.

References:

- https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main_classes/tokenizer


### SC4N-UNICODE-ANOMALY

**Text contains zero-width, Tags-block, bidi-control or homoglyph characters** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `content` · [CWE-1007](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1007.html), [CWE-838](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/838.html)

A string in the artifact contains characters that are invisible or that reverse text order: zero-width space/joiner/non-joiner, a character from the Unicode Tags block (U+E0000-U+E007F, the channel that spells an instruction a renderer drops and a tokeniser reads), the bidi control set, or a homoglyph mix of scripts in one identifier. These are how a card hides an instruction from a reader while a tokeniser still sees it, and how an identifier is made to look like an allowlisted one. Confidence is high because the characters are unambiguous; the severity is medium because the intent is not. Where the character is invisible the evidence names the rune or the block, because the character itself cannot be read in the report.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1007.html
- https://trojansource.codes/

## Repository-level supply chain

How to act on these: [`docs/triage.md#repo-supply-chain`](triage.md#repo-supply-chain).

### SC4N-GITATTRIBUTES-FILTER

**.gitattributes names a non-LFS filter or diff driver** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `gitattributes` · [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html), [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html)

A `.gitattributes` line assigns `filter=<driver>` or `diff=<driver>` for a driver other than LFS. A filter driver is configured in Git config with `clean`/`smudge` commands that Git executes when the file is checked out or staged, and a diff driver can name a `textconv` command executed on diff; the `.gitattributes` file only names the driver, so the command lives in the (attacker-influenced) local Git configuration. High because naming an unknown driver in a model repository is a request to run a program when the repository is cloned or diffed, and the known built-in diff drivers are allowlisted to keep syntax-highlighting conventions from firing the rule.

References:

- https://git-scm.com/docs/gitattributes
- https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#Documentation/git-config.txt-filterltdrivergtsmudge


### SC4N-GITATTRIBUTES-LFS

**.gitattributes routes files through Git LFS** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `gitattributes` · [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html)

A `.gitattributes` line assigns `filter=lfs` to a path pattern. Every matching file is then a small LFS *pointer* in the working tree, and the real content is fetched from the LFS server at checkout with no scanning by sc4n. Medium: it does not make an artifact malicious, but it is the reason a scan of a checkout can report a clean, tiny file that is not the artifact the loader will use. A repository whose weights are LFS pointers must be scanned from a fully materialised checkout or from the Hub blobs.

References:

- https://git-lfs.com/
- https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/security


### SC4N-HFCACHE-BLOB-MISSING

**Hugging Face cache snapshot entry has no blob** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `format` · [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)

A snapshot entry (or its symlink target) could not be stat'd. Either the link is dangling or the blob it names is absent, so the file contributes no bytes to the scan. Reporting it keeps a partially-populated cache from being mistaken for a fully-scanned one.


### SC4N-HFCACHE-REF-MALFORMED

**Hugging Face cache ref is not a commit hash** · severity `low` · confidence `high` · class `format` · [CWE-20](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html)

A file under refs/ does not contain a 40-hex commit hash. The refs are what label a blob with a human-meaningful revision in the report, so a malformed ref means a finding cannot be attributed to the revision the user was actually using. The blob is still scanned; only its label is missing.


### SC4N-HFCACHE-SYMLINK-ESCAPE

**Hugging Face cache symlink escapes the cache root** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `path` · [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html), [CWE-59](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/59.html)

A snapshot entry is a symlink that is absolute or whose target leaves the cache directory. The genuine cache layout uses relative links into ../../blobs, so an escaping link is either corruption or an attempt to make a model scan read a file outside the cache. sc4n resolves every link through os.Root and refuses to yield an entry that leaves the root, so the named file was NOT scanned; the finding records the request rather than the read.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/59.html


### SC4N-REPO-BUILD-BACKEND

**pyproject.toml names a build backend outside the known-good set** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `repo` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

The [build-system] build-backend is not one of the common, well-understood backends (setuptools.build_meta[:__legacy__], hatchling.build, flit_core.buildapi, poetry.core.masonry.api, maturin, scikit_build_core.build). PEP 517 imports and runs the named backend at build time, so an arbitrary backend name is code execution during build, before any package code is reviewed.

References:

- https://peps.python.org/pep-0517/
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-REPO-DOCKERFILE

**Dockerfile present in the scanned tree** · severity `medium` · confidence `low` · class `repo` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

A Dockerfile is present. A Dockerfile is executed when its image is built and it can fetch and run arbitrary code (RUN, ADD of a remote URL, base-image scripts). sc4n does not parse Dockerfiles; this finding exists so a container definition in a model repository is reviewed rather than overlooked.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-REPO-PTH

**Path configuration file executes code at interpreter start** · severity `critical` · confidence `high` · class `repo` · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

A .pth file has a line beginning with `import ` or `exec`. .pth files are not data: site.py executes any line that starts with `import` (or `import ` followed by a module with a `__main__`-style side effect) at the start of *every* interpreter run in that environment, with no import required. A .pth file inside a wheel is therefore code execution on install, and the reason a wheel in a model repository is scanned rather than trusted.

References:

- https://docs.python.org/3/library/site.html
- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html


### SC4N-REPO-PYC-ORPHAN

**Compiled .pyc has no .py source beside it** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `repo` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

A .pyc file with no sibling .py exists on disk. There is no source to lint, so whatever the bytecode does was not analysed; this is informational and does not by itself mean the bytecode is malicious, but a repository that ships only .pyc has nothing to review.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-REPO-SETUP-HOOK

**setup.py installs a custom command hook** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `repo` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

setup.py references cmdclass or defines one of the install/develop/build_py/sdist/egg_info/build_ext commands, or runs a shell/exec sink at module scope. A cmdclass entry replaces setuptools' own command, so the hook body runs during `pip install` with the installer's privileges; sc4n reports the trigger it saw. Ordinary setup.py files that only call setup() with metadata do not fire.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-REPO-SITE-CUSTOMIZE

**sitecustomize/usercustomize module runs at interpreter start** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `repo` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

A sitecustomize.py or usercustomize.py is present. Python imports sitecustomize (and usercustomize) automatically at startup, so whatever it contains runs in every interpreter in that environment without being imported by anything.

References:

- https://docs.python.org/3/library/site.html


### SC4N-REPO-SPACE-APP

**app.py present in the scanned tree** · severity `medium` · confidence `low` · class `repo` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

An app.py is present. app.py is the Gradio entry point a Hugging Face Space runs on container start, and the file a Space's build executes without the user opening it. sc4n does not parse the file here; the Python analyser covers its contents. This finding marks the entry point so a reviewer knows the tree is runnable rather than a static model directory.

References:

- https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/spaces-overview


### SC4N-REPO-START

**Python 3.15 startup entry point file executes a callable** · severity `critical` · confidence `high` · class `repo` · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

A file named *.start contains an entry point of the form `pkg.mod:callable`. Python 3.15+ executes these at interpreter startup, analogous to a .pth file but naming a callable directly, so the file is code that runs before the user's own program.

References:

- https://docs.python.org/3.15/whatsnew/3.15.html


### SC4N-REPO-WHEEL-IN-MODEL

**Python package archive found in the scanned tree** · severity `medium` · confidence `low` · class `repo` · [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html)

A .whl, .tar.gz or .tgz package archive sits in the scanned tree. A package archive installs code: it can ship a setup.py build hook, a .pth file or a .pyc. Its members are scanned separately as an archive, so this finding is the pointer to that scan, not a substitute for it — and the pointer is name-only, because telling an sdist from a dataset tarball needs the archive's members (a dataset.tar.gz and a diffsynth-1.0.tar.gz are the same bytes to a name test). Medium severity and low confidence for that reason: the same calibration as the name-driven Dockerfile and app.py pointers, where the content rules elsewhere in this package (a .pth line, a setup.py hook, a sitecustomize module) are the high and critical ones.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html


### SC4N-REPO-WORKFLOW-PRT

**GitHub workflow interpolates event data into a run step** · severity `high` · confidence `medium` · class `repo` · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

A .github/workflows file combines pull_request_target with a `run:` step that interpolates `${{ github.event.* }}`. pull_request_target runs with the base repository's secrets, and interpolating attacker-controlled event fields (a PR title, branch name or body) into a shell command is command injection into that privileged context. The match is textual (there is no YAML library linked), so it reports the co-occurrence rather than proving the interpolation reaches a shell.

References:

- https://securitylab.github.com/research/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/

## Coverage limits and dispatch

How to act on these: [`docs/triage.md#coverage-limits`](triage.md#coverage-limits).

### SC4N-FORMAT-AMBIGUOUS

**Format is ambiguous; content heuristic chose a parser** · severity `info` · confidence `low` · class `format`

More than one sniffer accepted this artifact's content, so the parser named in the evidence ran and the others did not. The probe that emits this today is the protobuf-shaped pair (ONNX, TF SavedModel, CoreML), where the wire format alone does not say which model description it is. If the artifact is the other member of the pair, its format-specific rules did not run.


### SC4N-FORMAT-EXTENSION-MISMATCH

**File content does not match its extension** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `format`

The bytes identify a different container than the file name implies. sc4n dispatched on the content, so the real format was still scanned; the finding matters because every extension-driven tool in the chain (and the human deciding whether to load the file) sees the name first and the format second. A .safetensors that is a zip, a .npz that is a tar and a .gguf that is a zip are documented evasion shapes. Where the pair is a real convention the extension is exempt and this rule stays silent: a .pt that is a 7z archive is the February 2025 campaign, reported as SC4N-TORCH-7Z, and a .bin that is a pickle is an ordinary torch save.

References:

- https://huggingface.co/blog/notable-models-scanned


### SC4N-INTERNAL-PANIC

**sc4n internal error while parsing (scanner bug)** · severity `low` · confidence `high` · class `structure` · [CWE-617](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/617.html)

A parser panicked and the panic was contained, so this artifact is only partially analysed. The panic is always a sc4n bug rather than a property of the artifact, and the evidence records the panic value; please report it with the artifact or a reduced reproducer. The remaining artifacts in the same run were still scanned.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/617.html


### SC4N-LIMIT-ARTIFACT

**File exceeds MaxArtifactBytes** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `limits` · [CWE-770](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html)

The file is larger than MaxArtifactBytes, so it was not opened. The path is reported as unreadable and the run exits 3. Either the file is genuinely outside the intended scan scope or it was inflated to push the scanner past its budget.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html


### SC4N-LIMIT-DECOMPRESSED

**Cumulative decompressed bytes exceed the cap** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `limits` · [CWE-409](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/409.html)

The archive decompressed to more than MaxDecompressedBytes in total. Scanning stopped at the cap, so later members were not analysed. Raise -max-decompress only on a host with the corresponding headroom.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/409.html


### SC4N-LIMIT-DEPTH

**Container nesting exceeds MaxDepth** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `limits` · [CWE-674](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/674.html)

The artifact nests containers (archive inside archive, or archive inside compression) deeper than MaxDepth allows, so scanning stopped at this level and the nested content was not analysed. Legitimate model repositories nest at most three levels (joblib inside gzip, a pickle inside a zip). A deeper nest is a way to move a payload past a depth-limited scanner, so treat this finding as "not fully scanned", not as "clean".

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/674.html


### SC4N-LIMIT-ENTRIES

**Element or member count exceeds its cap** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `limits` · [CWE-770](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html)

A count exceeded the cap that applies to it: an archive has more members than MaxEntries permits, or a metadata array (a GGUF vocabulary, a MessagePack or UBJSON container) has more elements than MaxArrayElements. The finding names the cap in its extra data. Whether the walk then stopped is stated in the evidence rather than implied here: some walks clamp the loop at the cap and say how many records they did not read, while others continue and report only the count. A very large count is the cheap way to exhaust a scanner's time or memory budget before it reaches the payload.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html


### SC4N-LIMIT-FINDINGS

**Finding count reached MaxFindings** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `limits`

The scan produced more findings than MaxFindings, so later findings were dropped and counted in the report's "dropped" summary field. Raise -max-findings to see all of them; the drop is always reported so a truncated finding list is never mistaken for a complete one.


### SC4N-LIMIT-HEADER

**Declared header exceeds MaxHeaderBytes** · severity `low` · confidence `high` · class `limits` · [CWE-770](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html)

A format's declared header or metadata region (the .npy header length, a TF-JS model.json, a safetensors header) is larger than MaxHeaderBytes, so it was truncated or rejected before analysis. The cap exists because the length field precedes the payload: a crafted value would otherwise make the parser read the whole file as a header.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html


### SC4N-LIMIT-RATIO

**Decompression ratio exceeds MaxRatio** · severity `high` · confidence `high` · class `limits` · [CWE-409](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/409.html)

One compression layer expands by more than MaxRatio (default 200:1). Two readings are possible and both are worth stopping at: a decompression bomb aimed at the scanner, or a member whose expansion is so large that the extracted payload cannot be analysed in memory. Decompression stopped at the cap, so the member is only partly analysed.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/409.html


### SC4N-LIMIT-RETAINED

**Retained text exceeds MaxRetainedText** · severity `low` · confidence `high` · class `limits` · [CWE-770](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html)

The parse has kept as much string/blob content alive as MaxRetainedText allows, so later values were recorded by length and kind without their text. Indicator matching still ran on each value as it was read; what is lost is the ability to re-inspect them later in the walk (and the evidence text for any finding that would have quoted them).

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html


### SC4N-LIMIT-SPILL

**Archive member exceeds MaxSpillBytes** · severity `medium` · confidence `high` · class `limits` · [CWE-770](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html)

A compressed archive member is larger than MaxSpillBytes, so it was not materialised for parsing. The member's own container checks (name, link, CRC) still ran; its *content* was not analysed, and the finding says so rather than leaving a reader to assume a clean member.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html


### SC4N-LIMIT-STRING

**String or blob exceeds MaxStringBlob** · severity `low` · confidence `high` · class `limits` · [CWE-770](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html)

A single declared string, metadata value or embedded blob is larger than MaxStringBlob, so it was truncated before analysis. Truncation is reported rather than silent: an indicator positioned after the truncation point would not be seen.

References:

- https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html


### SC4N-PARTIAL-SLICE

**Artifact is a header slice, so declared extents run past its end** · severity `info` · confidence `high` · class `structure` · [CWE-1059](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1059.html)

The scanner was given a byte prefix of a larger artifact (for example the first 2 MiB of a multi-gigabyte checkpoint, fetched under a per-file budget), and the format's declared extents therefore stop inside the slice. Nothing is wrong with the file: the structure was followed as far as the bytes go. Informational, because the consequence for a reviewer is coverage — what lies past the slice was not scanned, and a clean result for this artifact does not describe the whole file.

References:

- https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/security

## Weight statistics

How to act on these: [`docs/triage.md#weights-statistics`](triage.md#weights-statistics).

### SC4N-WEIGHTS-ALL-ZERO

**Tensor is entirely zero** · severity `info` · confidence `low` · class `weights`

Every sampled element of the tensor is zero. A zero tensor is legal (empty, masked or uninitialised heads exist in real checkpoints) but it is also where a payload rides unnoticed, so it is worth a human's eye. Informational, behind -deep-stats, never a gate.


### SC4N-WEIGHTS-DUPLICATE

**Tensor has an unusually high fraction of duplicate values** · severity `info` · confidence `low` · class `weights`

More than the configured fraction of a tensor's sampled elements repeat a value seen earlier in the sample. Duplicated rows/columns are how a naive backdoor injection copies a trigger weight set; they are also what quantisation, padding and a broadcast constant produce. Informational, behind -deep-stats, never a gate.


### SC4N-WEIGHTS-ENTROPY

**Tensor byte entropy is outside the expected band** · severity `info` · confidence `low` · class `weights`

The Shannon entropy of the tensor's sampled bytes is either very low (a large constant or zero region) or near the 8-bit maximum (compressed or encrypted data where weights should be). Both have benign explanations (a bias vector is low-entropy by construction; a deliberately encoded weight block is high-entropy). Informational, behind -deep-stats, never a gate.


### SC4N-WEIGHTS-NAN

**Tensor contains a high fraction of NaN or Inf values** · severity `info` · confidence `low` · class `weights`

More than the configured fraction of a tensor's sampled float values are NaN or +/-Inf. NaN/Inf weights are a real failure mode of broken training and a documented carrier for out-of-band signalling, but a freshly converted or partially written checkpoint can contain them too. Informational, behind -deep-stats, never a gate.


### SC4N-WEIGHTS-OUTLIER

**Tensor has magnitude outliers far above its own mean** · severity `info` · confidence `low` · class `weights`

More than the configured fraction of a tensor's sampled float elements have a magnitude larger than the configured multiple of the tensor's mean magnitude. A magnitude spike is the crudest backdoor signature and also a normal property of an untrained or clipped tensor. Informational, behind -deep-stats, never a gate.
